title: Shoppers start with AI while PC costs surge: our store must adapt
summary: 55% of consumers use AI in product discovery (NIQ); 34% would use GenAI for gift ideas (Gartner). Google opened Universal Cart; Walmart lets agents buy; Amazon blocks them. PC shipments fell 21% in Q3 and memory prices are rising.

points.headline: AI is becoming the front door to shopping, and retailers split on agent access
points.detail: NIQ finds 55% use AI in discovery; Google opened Universal Cart; Walmart allows agent purchases while Amazon blocks them. We should decide how our feeds and checkout treat agents.

points.headline: Payment networks are building trust rails for agent-made purchases
points.detail: American Express launched a framework to verify purchases by AI agents and Meta is pushing a shared shopping-agent standard. We should track standards and check payment readiness.

points.headline: PC demand is falling while memory shortages push prices up
points.detail: Counterpoint reports Q3 shipments down 21% with Q4 forecast worse, and record PC price inflation from memory costs. We should plan pricing, promotions and inventory for a weaker, costlier Q4.

points.headline: Holiday online demand is growing and channels are widening
points.detail: Adobe forecasts $275.1B in US online holiday sales, and Best Buy joined TikTok Shop. We should plan Cyber 5 deals and test new electronics channels.
